name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
definition: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct is a dense multilingual text instruction model developed by Meta in the Llama 3.3 family. It has 70B parameters, supports 128K tokens of context, accepts Text and produces Text. Its primary role is general-purpose multilingual chat, text generation and assistant workloads.

key_topics: general-purpose multilingual chat, text generation and assistant workloads

training.summary: Meta reports more than 15T pretraining tokens for the Llama 3 family and a December 2023 knowledge cutoff for Llama 3.3. The instruct checkpoint is aligned with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement-learning-based preference techniques.

license.special_conditions: Commercial and research use is intended, but the Community License and Acceptable Use Policy remain part of the deployment decision. Review the current official agreement for scale, attribution and redistribution conditions.
license.legal_note: OpenWeightModels summary for technical comparison; not legal advice.

deployments.notes: Widely used high-throughput serving path for Llama checkpoints.
Compatible server stack for large transformer inference.
Community GGUF/AWQ/GPTQ variants can reduce memory but require separate provenance checks.

hardware.summary: A dense 70B BF16 checkpoint is a multi-GPU or high-memory-server workload. Quantization can materially reduce weight memory, but long-context KV cache and throughput targets remain important.

limitations: Text-only model: no native image/audio input.
Performance in languages beyond the eight explicitly supported languages should be evaluated rather than assumed.
Custom Llama 3.3 licensing and acceptable-use terms remain part of production eligibility.
Static knowledge cutoff means current factual applications typically need retrieval or external data.
